name: Political instability
value: No G20 collapse; Indonesia VP vote 2 Dec
summary: Indonesia's assembly will elect a new vice-president on 2 Dec after the 12 Nov resignation; no G20 collapse found
state: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned on 12 Nov after a dispute over his diploma; the People's Consultative Assembly plans to elect a successor from two names put forward by President Prabowo on 2 Dec (The Star). Prabowo is to name his nominees after returning from the ASEAN and APEC summits, and no unrest was reported (InvestorTrust, 14 Nov). This is a constitutional succession, not a government collapse, and searches on 19 Nov found no G20 coup, contested election or collapse.
for_you: No direct effect for most readers. Travellers to Indonesia can follow FCDO travel advice for any updates around the 2 Dec vote.
rubric_hit: Normal: no G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month; Indonesia VP change is a scheduled assembly vote (2 Dec)

sources.title: The Star — Indonesia's upper house to pick new vice president on December 2, its speaker says

why: Coups, contested elections and constitutional crises in large economies unsettle markets, alliances and policy.
drivers: Elections, government collapses, coups, emergency rule, mass protest movements.

rubric.alert: Coup or constitutional crisis in a G20 country, or deadly unrest threatening a G20 government.
rubric.watch: Government collapse or contested election in a G20 country, or a coup anywhere.
rubric.normal: No G20 government collapse, contested election or coup in the past month.
